articles.title: Podocyte-derived palmitic acid drives p53 S-palmitoylation and CD103+ CD4+ T cell differentiation in humanized mouse model of systemic lupus erythematosus
Wt1 splice isoforms bias lineage programmes during formative pluripotency
articles.abstract: Abstract How transcriptional asymmetry arises in the epiblast before gastrulation remains a central question in mammalian development. Using a targeted CRISPRa screen, we identify Wt1 as a regulator of lineage-associated transcriptional programmes during formative pluripotency. Wt1 is transiently induced during formative pluripotency in vitro and in vivo, coincident with emerging lineage biases. Precocious Wt1 induction advances cells toward post-implantation identity, whereas Wt1 -deficient cells execute naïve exit but show impaired acquisition of formative and lineage-associated programmes. WT1 binds active regulatory elements together with OTX2, OCT4 and FOXO1. Comparison of Wt1 splice isoforms identifies KTS splice status as the major determinant of divergent anterior/neuroectodermal and posterior/mesodermal transcriptional programmes in vitro. In the E5.5 epiblast, Wt1 expression and splice composition align with lineage-biased states, linking isoform usage to anterior bias in vivo. Isoform-dependent programmes are conserved in human pluripotent cells. These findings identify alternative splicing as a mechanism tuning lineage-associated transcriptional bias before gastrulation.

Author Correction: Asian summer monsoon orbital variability directly paced by CO2 and precession, not eccentricity
Nitrene-triggered carbocationic rearrangement of tetrasubstituted alkenes enables divergent access to fused δ-lactams
articles.abstract: Abstract Transition-metal-catalyzed nitrene transfer has emerged as a powerful strategy for alkene functionalization, yet its application to sterically congested tetrasubstituted alkenes remains severely underdeveloped. Here, we report an Ir(III)-catalyzed nitrene-triggered aziridination–rearrangement cascade that enables the efficient conversion of cyclic-substituted tetrasubstituted alkenes into cycloalkane-fused δ-lactams. The transformation proceeds under mild conditions with excellent yields and uniformly high diastereoselectivities and exhibits broad compatibility with carbon-, oxygen-, and nitrogen-based nucleophiles, including structurally complex and biologically relevant substrates. Combined experimental and computational studies support a concerted aziridination by an Ir–nitrenoid to generate a strained tricyclic intermediate, which undergoes a strain-release-driven aza-semipinacol rearrangement to furnish a bicyclic azacarbocation. Divergent nucleophilic interception or elimination of this intermediate provides rapid access to structurally diverse fused δ-lactam architectures. These findings establish a nitrene-triggered carbocationic rearrangement manifold for the functionalization of tetrasubstituted alkenes and expand the synthetic potential of transition-metal-catalyzed nitrene transfer.

Waste as Feedstock,
Electrolyte, and Target: Closing
the Loop in Electrochemical H2O2 Water Treatment
articles.abstract: Abstract Electrochemical H2O2 production is increasingly positioned as an on-site route for water oxidation, disinfection, and resource recovery. However, its environmental translation remains constrained by a basic design mismatch between catalyst development in clean electrolytes and deployment in chemically variable waste streams. This Perspective argues that progress should move beyond catalyst-centered performance metrics toward a closed-loop, waste-centered framework. The key issue is not how to isolate H2O2 electrosynthesis from wastewater complexity but when and how that complexity can be engineered. Solid and liquid waste streams can provide carbon, heteroatoms, and metals for impurity-resilient electrodes. Meanwhile, wastewater constituents can regulate interfacial ion distribution, water structure, oxygen transport, proton availability, intermediate stabilization, and side reactions. Electrogenerated H2O2 can be routed to contaminant transformation, disinfection, detoxification, and metal recovery. We discuss design principles for converting heterogeneous waste feedstocks into catalytic interfaces, defining wastewater operating windows, matching reactor architectures with real water matrices, and evaluating circularity through life-cycle and techno-economic accounting. We identify critical benchmarks─matrix descriptors, durability mechanisms, byproduct control, reactor-treatment matching, and transparent environmental safeguards─needed to turn circular H2O2 concepts into verifiable water-treatment technologies.

articles.title:
Light-Induced Formation
of Volatile Organic Compounds
from Bleach Cleaning in Indoor Environments
articles.abstract: Abstract Surface bleach cleaning is a common indoor activity that releases abundant strong oxidants, including hypochlorous acid (HOCl) and chlorine gas (Cl2), which can significantly influence indoor chemistry. While bleach-driven chemical transformations are recognized, the specific role of illumination remains poorly understood. This study combines field measurements and laboratory flow tube experiments to investigate volatile organic compound (VOC) formation from reactions between bleach emissions and surface-sorbed species, e.g., kitchen-derived organic films, under illuminated conditions. In real-world indoor settings, we observed that bleach cleaning under light predominantly generates oxygenated VOCs (OVOCs), accounting for ∼92% of total emissions. Saturated carbonyls contributed the most (∼82%), such as C6H12O, C9H18O, and C2H4O. Flow tube experiments using surrogate compounds and kitchen-collected surface films confirmed that OVOCs are generated via heterogeneous reactions between surface-bound organics (e.g., fatty acids, amides, amino acids) and radicals produced from photolysis of bleach-derived oxidants. VOC production was found to depend on surface accumulation and aging, with more accumulated and aged surfaces producing greater quantities and more diverse products. These findings provide important insights into VOC production from indoor surface chemistry initiated by bleach cleaning under typical indoor lighting conditions, advancing our understanding of volatile byproduct formation from indoor bleach photochemistry.

articles.title:
Coal
Tar-Based Driveway Sealant Extract Induces Mutations
in Liver, Bone Marrow, and Germ Cells of MutaMouse Male Mice
articles.abstract: Abstract Coal tar-based driveway sealants (CTS) are a widespread but underrecognized source of human exposure to mutagenic polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs). We used Duplex Sequencing, an error-corrected sequencing technology, to assess the mutagenicity of a complex PAH mixture extracted from a CTS in MutaMouse male mice. We observed significant dose-dependent increases in mutation frequency (MF) in liver and bone marrow, with mutation spectra dominated by C:G > A:T substitutions, closely resembling a mutational signature linked to human cancers associated with tobacco smoking. In germ cells, we did not observe a statistically significant increase in MF, although there was a positive dose–response trend and enrichment of C:G > A:T mutations at higher doses. The mutagenic effects of CTS in germ cells were supported by a statistically significant increase in mutant frequency measured using the plaque-based lacZ assay. Tissue-specific analyses revealed greater mutation susceptibility and potency in liver, likely reflecting its central role in PAH metabolism. Mutation spectrum analysis showed that the mutagenic profile of the CTS extract largely resembled that of benzo(a)pyrene; however, detailed spectral analysis indicated additional contributions from other PAHs or PAH metabolites that produced distinct mutational patterns. Collectively, our findings demonstrate that the CTS extract induces tissue-specific mutagenic responses driven by characteristic C:G > A:T mutations, offering mechanistic insight into how environmental PAH mixtures contribute to mutation burden and cancer risk.

articles.title:
Ion
Valence Difference Governs Membrane Charge Preference
in Nanofiltration-Based Radionuclide Separation
articles.abstract: Abstract Selective separation of radionuclides with varying environmental hazards is critical for mitigating the disposal burden of high-level radioactive wastewater. Although positively charged (PC) membranes are generally considered effective for cation pair separation, the applicability of negatively charged (NC) membranes for separating cations with large valence differences remains unresolved. In this study, Ag+/Zr4+ and Ag+/Sr2+ were used as representative radionuclides with large and small valence differences, respectively, to evaluate the separation performance and underlying mechanisms of PC and NC membranes. Notably, NC membranes maintained near-complete rejection of Zr4+ while simultaneously exhibiting higher Ag+ permeability, thereby achieving superior Ag+/Zr4+ selectivity relative to PC membranes. DFT calculations and MD simulations revealed that strong ion–membrane interactions facilitated preferential partitioning of Zr4+ at the NC membrane interface, whereas differences in hydration energy governed the competitive transport of Ag+ and Zr4+. Furthermore, Zr4+ accumulated at the membrane surface induced incomplete dehydration of Ag+, reducing interfacial transport barriers and promoting Ag+ permeation. Comparative analysis of Ag+/Zr4+ and Ag+/Sr2+ systems further demonstrated that ion valence difference governs the preference of membrane charges: NC membranes are preferred for M+/M4+ separations, whereas PC membranes are preferred for M+/M2+ separations, which was further validated by Li+/Mg2+ and Li+/Ti4+ separations. These findings clarify the mechanistic distinction between co-ion and counterion competition, providing guidance for the selection of membrane charge types for energy-efficient radionuclide separation and selective resource recovery beyond the nuclear industry.

articles.title:
Source
or Sink: Bioanalytical and Chemical Profiling
of New and Field-Weathered Plastics
articles.abstract: Abstract Plastics contain complex mixtures of chemicals that can leach into the aquatic environment. Conversely, the high sorption capacity of certain polymers renders plastics passive samplers for environmental pollutants from ambient waters. We evaluated whether effects from chemicals that are extractable or leachable from plastics from the North Pacific Ocean are dominated by plastic-associated or sorbed environmental compounds. First, bioanalytical profiling of chemical mixtures from solvent extracts of field-weathered marine plastics in cell-based bioassays was compared to that of chemicals from solvent extracts of newly purchased counterparts of the field plastics. Second, the new plastics were artificially UV-weathered and solvent-extracted, and the leachate waters were enriched with solid-phase extraction and dosed into a test battery of four in vitro bioassays where activation of the arylhydrocarbon receptor, oxidative stress response, and/or cytotoxicity were most responsive. Finally, chemical screening was performed using high-resolution mass spectrometry with subsequent mixture effect modeling to identify toxicity drivers. The results showed a multifaceted picture: Newly purchased high-durability outdoor products caused higher effects before weathering, whereas food packaging tended to show increased effects after field weathering. The analyzed chemicals could partially explain the observed effects (<0.1–98%). Our study underlines the relevance of field weathering for marine plastics and their potential to leach chemicals of concern into the environment.

articles.title:
Soil Mineral Coatings
on Biodegradable Microplastics:
Formation and Control of Enzymatic Degradation
articles.abstract: Abstract In agriculture, biodegradable plastics weather and fragment into microplastics that inevitably acquire mineral coatings. However, the impact of mineral coatings on microplastic degradation remains poorly understood. We examined coating formation and enzymatic degradation of pristine and photoaged poly(butylene adipate-co-terephthalate) microplastics (PBAT-MPs) in loessial soil and red soil under drought, moist, alternate wetting-drying, and flooded regimes during 64 days. Soil type, moisture, and photoaging governed coating accumulation. Loessial soil produced greater Al and Fe loading on PBAT-MPs than red soil, while unsaturated regimes increased Al and Fe by 394%–1109% relative to flooding (p < 0.05). Synchrotron micro-X-ray fluorescence combined with absorption near-edge structure spectroscopy analyses showed heterogeneous elemental distributions and mineral speciation on PBAT-MPs that resembled those of the source soils. Unexpectedly, loessial-soil coatings increased PBAT-MPs’ terephthalic acid and adipic acid release by 9.1%–17.4% and reduced residual PBAT mass by 6.5%–23.5% (p < 0.05). Kinetic analyses showed that although mineral coatings slowed enzyme adsorption via diffusion limitations, localized leaching of Ca2+ from the coatings enhanced cutinase activity and outweighed this physical constraint. These findings demonstrate that mineral coatings can regulate the enzymatic degradation of PBAT, providing new insights into the environmental fate of biodegradable microplastics in agricultural soils.

articles.title:
Molecular Interactions
between Styrene Oligomers and
Human Serum Albumin: A Multiscale Computational Study of a Plastic-Derived
Environmental Contaminant
articles.abstract: Abstract Micro- and nanoplastics are pervasive environmental pollutants known to accumulate in human organs. While the hazards of larger plastic particles are under intense investigation, the toxicological impact of molecular-level plastic oligomers with dimensions around 1 nm is a critical and underexplored area. This study provides a comprehensive molecular-level in silico characterization of the binding interactions between styrene oligomers (1–7 units) and HSA, characterizing their molecular basis and its potential relevance to HSA’s ligand transport function. A multilevel computational approach was employed, integrating molecular docking, MD simulations, DFT, MM/PBSA binding free energy calculations, and ProLIF interaction fingerprinting. FA1 accommodated 82–95% of the most favorable docking poses for oligomers containing three to seven styrene units and exhibited the lowest docking scores, reaching −11.9 kcal·mol–1, compared with −6.4 kcal·mol–1 for the monomer. MD simulations confirmed the structural stability of oligomer-HSA complexes, further supported by dynamic cross-correlation, principal component, and solvent-accessible surface area analyses. Quantum biochemistry analyses further confirmed FA1 as the most energetically favorable binding pocket, with an average interaction energy of −117.47 kcal·mol–1 compared with −73.96 kcal·mol–1 for FA6, a hierarchy independently reproduced by MM/PBSA calculations (R = 0.82). For the hexamer and heptamer, FA1 exhibited energetic advantages of 27.39 and 21.84 kcal·mol–1, respectively. These findings indicate that HSA binds styrene oligomers with high stability and affinity at FA1, providing a molecular basis for further investigation of their potential relevance to ligand transport and systemic exposure to plastic-derived contaminants.

articles.title:
Spatially
Coupled
•H-involved Reductive Decomplexation
of Cu(II)–EDTA for Sludge-Free Copper Recovery
articles.abstract: Abstract The electrochemical recovery of metals from stable complexes is often limited by the accessibility of coordinated metal centers at the electrode interface. Here, we develop a polyaniline-modified carbon felt (PANI@CF) cathode to regulate the interfacial microenvironment for selective Cu recovery from copper(II)–ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (Cu(II)–EDTA). The PANI interface couples Cu(II)–EDTA enrichment with •H generation through complementary nitrogen functionalities, thereby promoting Cu(II)–EDTA decomplexation while preserving ligand integrity. Under optimized conditions, PANI@CF achieves high Cu recovery (up to 99.9%) over a broad Cu(II)–EDTA concentration range (0.5–5 mM) and pH range (3–11), with a 32.75-fold enhancement in the apparent reaction rate compared with pristine carbon felt. Mechanistic investigations reveal that imine (–N═) functionalities contribute to interfacial Cu(II)–EDTA enrichment, whereas amine (–NH–) functionalities facilitate N–H activation and •H generation. This spatial coupling promotes interactions between short-lived •H and coordinated Cu centers, weakening Cu(II)–EDTA coordination and facilitating Cu reduction while preserving EDTA integrity. After ten consecutive treatment cycles, the cumulative Cu recovery reached 215.07 mg cm–2, and the PANI@CF electrode was regenerated by mild acid washing. The selective recovery of Cu and EDTA was further demonstrated in actual electroplating wastewater. This work highlights interfacial regulation through spatial coupling as a strategy for overcoming accessibility limitations in the electrochemical transformation of metal–ligand complexes and supports selective resource recovery from complexed industrial effluents.

articles.title:
Evaluating
Individual
Infection Risk: The Interplay
between Air Mixing Intensities and Occupant Dynamics
articles.abstract: Abstract Aerosol transmission remains a critical route for the spread of respiratory infectious diseases, yet real-time exposure mapping in complex public spaces is computationally demanding. This study presents a robust and adaptable framework for estimating dynamic individual exposure (i.e., viral dose) by integrating high-fidelity computational fluid dynamics (CFD) with computer vision (CV) analysis. By overlaying validated steady-state viral aerosol plumes onto dynamic human interaction data, we evaluated the interplay between airflow patterns and human behaviors under two distinct air change rates (ACH: 25 h–1 and 3 h–1). Each scenario was simulated both with and without MERV-13 filtration. Applications in both a stochastic-movement hotel meeting room and a stationary-occupant office demonstrate that while high turbulence due to high ACH limits the spatial extent of plumes, sustained close proximity in structured settings can result in disproportionately high viral doses for specific individuals. MERV-13 filtration effectively reduced exposure within high-concentration zones. We propose a Reynolds number (Re)-based modeling guideline: steady-state CFD-CV for moderate mixing (900 ≤ Re ≤ 2300), a well-mixed assumption for high mixing (Re > 2300), and transient CFD-CV for low mixing (500 ≤ Re < 900) during breathing and speaking, and steady-state CFD-CV for coughing and sneezing regardless of Re value. This framework supports real-time monitoring and targeted interventions, providing a data-driven foundation for indoor occupant safety.

articles.title:
UV328 Promotes Plastisphere
Formation on Microplastics
through Quorum-Sensing-Associated Signaling Interference
articles.abstract: Abstract Microplastics have created an expanding anthropogenic microbial niche known as the plastisphere, yet the mechanisms by which plastic additives influence these microbial assemblies remain poorly understood. Here, we show that UV328, a ubiquitous benzotriazole stabilizer recently listed in the Stockholm Convention, may be associated with quorum sensing signaling that accelerates plastisphere formation, biomass accumulation, and extracellular polymeric substance production on microplastics. In UV328-exposed polystyrene and polylactic acid plastisphere, the total expression levels of biofilm formation genes are upregulated by 1.38- to 2.94-fold compared to the control and quorum quenching manipulations. Molecular dynamics simulations predict that UV328 structurally mimics N-acyl-homoserine lactone (AHL) and may plausibly occupy ligand-binding domains of the quorum sensing receptor SdiA and CciR with favorable energetics. UV328 exposure was further associated with the upregulation of genes involved in bacterial chemotaxis, flagellar assembly, and central carbon metabolism. This physiological reprogramming alters community assembly trajectories and leads to a protein-rich plastisphere phenotype that was reversible by enzymatic quorum quenching, potentially supporting the involvement of AHL-sensitive processes. Our findings suggest that UV328 can alter plastisphere development through signaling-associated ecological processes, raising the possibility that microplastics may function as chemically active interfaces and highlighting microbial signaling interference as an overlooked dimension of the ecological risks associated with plastic additives in aquatic ecosystems.

articles.title:
Ammonia
Triggers
Interfacial Breakpoint Chlorination
to Enhance Micropollutant Degradation and Reshapes Chlorinated Byproduct
Formation during Electrochlorination
articles.abstract: Abstract Electrochlorination is a promising technology for micropollutant degradation in decentralized water treatment. However, ammonia can alter chlorine chemistry. This study investigates the effect of ammonia on micropollutant degradation and chlorinated byproduct formation during electrochlorination using the RuO2/IrO2–Ti anode. Compared to electrochlorination at 10 mM chloride without ammonia, the presence of 1 mM ammonia increased the degradation rate constants of metronidazole and carbamazepine by 2.7- and 4.5-fold, respectively. This enhancement is consistent with interfacial breakpoint chlorination, defined as preferential chlorine–ammonia conversion within an anode-adjacent, chlorine-rich aqueous diffusion layer before complete bulk mixing. During electrochlorination with ammonia, dissolved HO• contributed to micropollutant degradation. Electron paramagnetic resonance provided qualitative evidence of HO• formation, whereas nitrobenzene was used as a probe to quantify its steady-state concentration. The ammonia-induced steady-state HO• concentration reached 2.4 × 10–13 M at 1 mM ammonia, whereas the HO• contribution was negligible without ammonia. Meanwhile, 1–5 mM ammonia reduced the total yields of chlorinated byproducts by only 25–31% during electrochlorination. The limited suppression is consistent with concurrent competition between ammonia and dissolved organic matter for locally generated chlorine within the anode-adjacent region. These findings identify near-anode chlorine–ammonia conversion as a route to reactive-species formation and micropollutant degradation, while showing that chlorinated byproducts remain a concern in ammonia-containing electrochlorination systems.

articles.title:
Suppressing
Proton Affinity of Surface Oxygen for
Enhanced N2 Selectivity in Mn-Based NH3–SCR
Catalysts
articles.abstract: Abstract Inferior N2 selectivity remains a critical challenge for Mn-based catalysts in NH3–SCR denitration. Here, using atomically dispersed Mn on anatase (Mn1/TiO2) and MnO2 as model catalysts, we elucidate the origin of surface oxygen activity and the role of surface oxygen in the formation of N2O. Both catalysts achieved >99% NO conversion in the temperature range of 175–300 °C (WHSV = 60,000 mL·g–1·h–1). Compared with the poor selectivity of α-MnO2 (1.2% at 300 °C), Mn1/TiO2 maintained >88.0% N2 selectivity in 50–300 °C. Density functional theory calculations revealed that the high affinity of surface oxygen for protons results in overoxidation of NH3-derived intermediates, thus promoting N2O formation. Orbital interaction analysis manifested that surface oxygen activity in octahedrally coordinated catalysts depends on the spin polarization in transition-metal 3d bands. Atomic dispersion of Mn sites on oxides with nonspin-polarized dxy orbitals was demonstrated as a universal strategy to boost N2 selectivity. This work deepens the fundamental understanding of surface oxygen activity in catalysts, paving a way for designing Mn-based catalysts with excellent N2 selectivity.

articles.title:
Mild Oxidant Regulation
of *H Coverage Promotes Electrocatalytic
Nitrate Reduction to N2 in Low-Conductivity Media
articles.abstract: Abstract Electrocatalytic nitrate reduction reaction (NO3RR) has attracted growing interest for converting nitrate (NO3–) into ammonium (NH4+), yet NH4+ production from dilute, low-conductivity waters is constrained by high energy consumption, limited NO3– availability, and costly product recovery. Steering NO3RR directly toward benign N2 therefore represents a more practical route, but this pathway is often suppressed by excessive surface *H coverage, which drives the overhydrogenation of nitrogen intermediates to NH4+. Here, we report a mild oxidant-assisted coelectrolysis strategy that regulates interfacial *H coverage and promotes NO3–-to-N2 conversion in a Cu nanoparticle-decorated Ni cathode membrane electrochemical reactor. This reactor separates a highly conductive electrochemical chamber from a NO3–-containing chemical chamber, enabling NO3– reduction in low-conductivity media while maintaining a less negative cathodic potential. Mild oxidants, including H2O2, O2, CH3COOOH, and KIO4, consumed excess *H and redirected the reaction pathway toward N–N coupling. With H2O2 as a representative oxidant, N2 selectivity increased from 13.47% without H2O2 to 87.25% at 100 mM H2O2. Mechanistic analyses revealed that H2O2 decreases interfacial *H abundance, which suppresses NH4+ formation and facilitates the dimerization of nitrogen-containing intermediates. Verification in real low-conductivity groundwater further supports this strategy as a mechanistic basis for designing selective, low-energy electrochemical denitrification systems for low-conductivity NO3–-contaminated media.

articles.title:
Interfacial Triplet-Energy
Funneling Directs Energy-Transfer-Mediated
Singlet Oxygen Generation for Deep Toluene Mineralization
articles.abstract: Abstract Photocatalytic oxidation is a promising strategy for volatile organic compounds (VOCs) abatement, but incomplete mineralization and carbonaceous intermediate accumulation remain major challenges, especially when conventional charge-transfer pathways generate nonselective radical reactive oxygen species. Selective activation of molecular oxygen toward singlet oxygen (1O2) offers a potential route to controlled oxidation, yet efficient energy-transfer-mediated 1O2 generation in solid-state photocatalysts remains difficult to achieve. Herein, a strongly coupled In(OH)3/ZnGa2O4 heterojunction with an electronic structure consistent with an S-scheme configuration is constructed to investigate interfacial excited-state regulation. Spectroscopic measurements indicate modified excited-state relaxation and a reduced effective singlet–triplet energy separation, which may favor singlet-to-triplet conversion. Combined spectroscopic analyses, quenching experiments, and density functional theory calculations support a proposed interfacial triplet-energy-funneling pathway involving ZnGa2O4-related/interfacial triplet-related states and subsequent energy transfer to adsorbed O2 for 1O2 generation. As a result, the optimized In(OH)3/ZnGa2O4 photocatalyst achieves 98.3% toluene removal and 92.4% mineralization in a continuous-flow gas-phase reactor, together with excellent cycling stability and humidity tolerance. Mechanistic results further suggest that a pathway involving 1O2 contributes to methyl oxidation and the subsequent conversion of oxygenated intermediates, potentially limiting carbonaceous residue accumulation. This work provides an excited-state-engineering strategy for selective molecular oxygen activation and offers a promising route toward efficient, durable, and deeply mineralizing photocatalytic VOCs abatement.

articles.title:
Global Steel Decarbonization
under Policy, Technology,
and Resource Constraints: A Process-Unit Agent-Based Model
articles.abstract: Abstract Deep decarbonization of steel requires low-emission technologies to be deployed through a long-lived and heterogeneous asset fleet without disrupting steel supply. We developed a country-resolved agent-based model that follows global steel process units annually from 2023 to 2060. Units choose among continued operation, renewal, retrofit, conversion, retirement, and new construction, subject to construction time, linked upstream capacity, national production pathways, and annual supplies of scrap, hydrogen, natural gas, and pellets. Four scenarios distinguish stronger climate policy from improved technology and resource availability. Global process-chain CO2 emissions decline by 67–79% by 2060, reaching 0.476–0.737 Gt. The integrated case achieves the lowest emissions, but the two-component interventions do not independently outperform the reference case. Stronger policy changes when assets enter a finite transition queue, whereas technology and material conditions determine whether replacement routes can be built and operated at that time. By 2060, Scrap-EAF supplies 74–80% of crude steel, but residual unabated blast furnaces and coal-based direct reduction keep national steel pathways above their allocated levels in many countries. Deep decarbonization, therefore, depends on coordinating asset turnover, construction, and complementary material systems, rather than on technology availability or carbon-price pressure alone.

articles.title:
Mechanistic
Insights
into Humic Acid-Mediated Photosensitized
Activation of Mn(VII) under UVA Irradiation
articles.abstract: Abstract Ultraviolet A/permanganate [UVA/Mn(VII)] is a promising advanced oxidation process (AOP), while few studies have noticed that humic acid (HA) could enhance microcontaminant degradation in the process. For the first time, the promotive effect of HA and the underlying mechanisms were investigated in UVA/Mn(VII). HA significantly enhanced the generation of hydroxyl radical (HO•) and reactive manganese species (RMnS). Consequently, the pseudo-first-order reaction rate constants for microcontaminant degradation in UVA/Mn(VII)/HA were several to tens of times those in UVA/Mn(VII). The promotive effect of HA was attributed to the enhanced Mn(VII) activation by photogenerated reactive intermediates derived from irradiated HA. Among them, the excited triplet state of HA (3HA*) played a major role, which was also supported by benzophenone (BP), a model triplet state photosensitizer. The second-order reaction rate constants of Mn(VII) with 3HA* and 3BP* were determined to be 2.54(±0.31) × 108 and 2.88(±0.10) × 109 M–1 s–1, respectively. Spectroscopic analysis and theoretical calculations supported an electron transfer mechanism for the reactions of Mn(VII) with 3HA* and 3BP*. Mn(VII) accepted one electron from 3HA*/3BP* and was reduced to Mn(VI), which underwent disproportionation to form Mn(VII) and Mn(V), followed by HO• and other RMnS generation. These findings provide novel perspectives for the application of UVA/Mn(VII) in practical water treatment.

articles.title:
Implementation Gap
in Global Power Capacity Expansion
to meet Paris Agreement Climate Targets
articles.abstract: Abstract Meeting the Paris Agreement’s climate targets demands an unprecedented expansion of renewable energy. Despite global commitments, significant implementation gaps persist due to economic, policy, and technical uncertainties. Here, we develop a Global Power Capacity Dynamics Framework, integrating facility-level data, machine learning and transition modeling to assess the feasibility of global power expansion. Analyzing 215,849 power plant units across five status modes (operating, planned, canceled, standby, retired), the framework explicitly incorporates the likelihood of planned capacity realization and the conversion of existing fossil assets. We find that by 2030, only 51% [40%–61%] of announced planned capacity is expected to become operational, while 26% [19%–36%] is likely to be canceled, with fossil fuel projects, especially coal, facing a cancellation rate of about 35%. Global operational capacity is projected to reach 9727 GW [9626–9848], including 178 GW [159–198] of existing fossil units requiring conversion or replacement (e.g., coal-to-gas, fossil-to-biomass). Although renewables dominate the planned pipeline, they are projected to constitute only 52% of the global energy mix by 2030, well below levels needed to meet climate goals. Regional disparities are pronounced: Asia, despite its relatively low cancellation rate, faces the world’s largest implementation gap, requiring an additional 2488 GW of solar and contending with 523 GW of stranded coal capacity to remain on a 1.5 °C pathway. This study provides the first probabilistic, facility-level assessment of global power capacity trajectories, revealing critical shortfalls in planned deployment and underscoring the urgency of aligning capacity expansion with climate targets.

articles.title:
Carbon Source Diversity
Shapes DOM Chemodiversity
and Antibiotic Resistome in Earthworm Casts
articles.abstract: Abstract The earthworm gut acts as a hotspot for reprocessing ingested organic matter, thereby altering carbon availability. These changes reshape microbial communities and competitive interactions, potentially affecting the dissemination of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in the gut. Beyond substrate amount, substrate diversity shapes these processes, yet its role remains unknown. We established microcosm experiments with a substrate-diversity gradient, combining FT-ICR MS and metagenomics to investigate dissolved organic matter (DOM) chemistry, microbial traits and ARGs in earthworm guts. Higher substrate diversity enriched carbon-centered metabolic genes and increased gut DOM availability, possibly through the proliferation of polysaccharide-degrading microorganisms with larger genomes. However, higher carbon availability may have increased microbial nutrient demand, accompanied by reductions in CHON-containing compounds and stronger microbial competition. ARG enrichment was associated with greater potential for microbial competition, as indicated by stronger negative microbial interactions and higher competition indices derived from genome scale metabolic models. In vitro monoculture of gut-derived pathogenic Klebsiella pneumoniae showed that substrate diversity enriched multidrug- and β-lactam-resistance genes and reshaped the resistome. Collectively, these findings suggest that increased substrate diversity modifies earthworm-driven carbon reprocessing, may reshape microbial resource competition and promote ARG enrichment, providing insights into the linkage between organic matter processing and resistome in soil fauna.

articles.title:
Market-Average Data
Can Misrepresent Supply Chain
Environmental Impacts and Their Uncertainty
articles.abstract: Abstract Market-average data sets are often used in life cycle assessment and carbon accounting when the production route of a procured good is unknown. The uncertainty this introduces is commonly characterized using generic pedigree matrix factors, which do not reflect how variability across production geographies and technologies differs between goods. Here, we develop a hybrid method that combines pedigree matrix uncertainty characterization within individual production routes with market-share-weighted Monte Carlo sampling between known production routes to represent uncertainty about which route supplied the good. We compare it with conventional market-average uncertainty analysis for 30 economically important goods. For climate impacts, conventional 5th–95th interpercentile intervals are narrower than route-weighted sampling intervals for 25 goods, at least 50% narrower for 14 goods, and up to 82% narrower. Conventional intervals exclude the central climate impact estimates of 44% of possible production routes. Route-weighted sampling captures these outcomes and reveals multimodality and impact-category-specific uncertainty profiles that conventional analysis does not. Variance decomposition distinguishes geographical and technological differences between routes from uncertainty within routes, helping prioritize supplier data collection. These differences show that conventional uncertainty estimates can mislead and may not capture how substantially initial estimates could change when supplier-specific data become available.

articles.title: Issue Publication Information
